startup_copy.evidence: The startup loop loads source, destination and end, then copies 32-bit words until destination reaches end.

points.name: system.apps.kill
points.prototype: uint32_t(const char *requester, uint32_t reason, const char *package)

evidence: The startup data contains Thumb pointers to the page, app and back navigation functions. Many system pages load this shared table at 0x200eb6e0 and call these slots with a pointer to a 44-byte navigation action. The page and app implementations read target fields and return 0 or 1; the back implementation logs navigate_back. Runtime pointer attach checks the live slot against its expected initialized value before publishing an aligned pointer store.
limitations: The data-copy result describes startup, not a guarantee that no firmware component overwrites the slot later. The action pointer and embedded page/app names, parameters and callbacks must remain valid according to the actual caller. Navigation and app termination affect system state; altering or skipping them can disrupt normal operation. Direct calls to the original implementation bypass the table slot. Atomic slot publication and retained callback dispatchers do not establish system-wide quiescence or make runtime unload safe. No device validation.
additional_evidence: The finish slot extracts an action page ID or resolves a page name, then calls finish_page; null action selects the current top page.
The home wrapper forwards a mode word to a routine constructing a home action and calling the background-page slot; zero and nonzero choose different transition callbacks.
The background-page implementation logs navigate_page_with_background and forwards the action to the page manager.

The kill-background wrapper forwards requester and reason unchanged to activitymanager_kill_bg_apps; the battery long-endurance path calls it with requester settings_battery and reason 0. Its return can be a log function return, so do not assume it is a boolean.
The kill-app wrapper forwards requester, reason and package unchanged to activitymanager_kill_app; one observed call uses snap, 0 and com.xiaomi.miwear.breath.

page_id.evidence: The page navigation implementation loads the combined word at +4 as a page target. Callers initialize the low halfword as page ID.

app_id.evidence: Page and app navigation implementations read a halfword at +6 and pass it as an app identifier to the app lookup.

source.evidence: Page and app navigation implementations load the byte at +8 and pass it to the start-source setter, which clamps it and stores it at 0x200eb6dc.

action_fields.limitations: These fields are for the currently observed 44-byte action passed through the named table slots. Null action is allowed by finish_page. The source byte is an input to a clamp, not necessarily the stored source. Lifetimes and other fields are caller-dependent; no device validation.
